description: 20 engineering proposals with known answers. 10 contain a clear physical or technical flaw (expected: reject); 10 are sound (expected: approve). 'why' is the human reasoning and is never sent to the model.

cases.proposal: A remote air-quality station draws 50 W continuously, 24 hours a day. We will power it with a single 20 W solar panel and no battery.
cases.why: Needs 1,200 Wh/day; a 20 W panel makes roughly 100 Wh/day and nothing at night.

cases.proposal: Mount a 300 W GPU server inside a fully sealed, airtight plastic enclosure with no fans, vents or heat sink, outdoors in a desert.
cases.why: 300 W of heat has nowhere to go; the box will overheat.

cases.proposal: Stream live 4K video at 25 Mbps from a farm camera to the cloud, using LoRaWAN as the only network link.
cases.why: LoRaWAN carries at most tens of kbps, about 1,000x too little.

cases.proposal: Run a 60 W motor for 5 hours from one 12 V, 2 Ah lead-acid battery.
cases.why: Needs 300 Wh; the battery holds about 24 Wh.

cases.proposal: Guarantee a 1 ms round-trip latency between servers in Hangzhou and New York over optical fibre.
cases.why: Light in fibre needs well over 100 ms for that round trip.

cases.proposal: Each sensor gateway records 10 TB of raw data per day onto a single 64 GB SD card, which is offloaded once a week.
cases.why: 70 TB per week into 64 GB.

cases.proposal: A quadcopter whose four motors give 2 kg of total thrust will carry a 3 kg camera. The frame itself weighs 1 kg.
cases.why: 4 kg of weight against 2 kg of thrust: it cannot take off.

cases.proposal: Charge a 75 kWh electric car battery from empty to full in 5 minutes using a 7 kW home wall charger.
cases.why: At 7 kW this takes over 10 hours.

cases.proposal: Serve a 70-billion-parameter language model in full FP16 precision on a single GPU with 24 GB of memory, with no offloading.
cases.why: FP16 weights alone need about 140 GB.

cases.proposal: Power a water pump with a generator that is driven by the same water the pump lifts, so the system runs forever with no outside energy.
cases.why: Perpetual motion; violates conservation of energy.

cases.proposal: A 10 W sensor node runs 24/7 in a sunny region (about 5 peak sun hours per day), powered by a 100 W solar panel and a 500 Wh LiFePO4 battery.
cases.why: Needs 240 Wh/day; panel gives roughly 350-500 Wh/day; battery covers about 2 days.

cases.proposal: Cool a 65 W desktop CPU inside a ventilated office PC case using a tower air cooler rated for 150 W.
cases.why: Cooler has more than 2x headroom.

cases.proposal: Send one 50-byte soil-moisture reading every 10 minutes from 100 farm sensors over LoRaWAN to a single gateway 2 km away.
cases.why: Tiny, infrequent packets are exactly what LoRaWAN is for.

cases.proposal: Keep a 10 W Wi-Fi router running for 4 hours during power cuts using a 12 V, 20 Ah LiFePO4 battery and an efficient DC-DC converter.
cases.why: Needs 40 Wh; battery holds about 240 Wh.

cases.proposal: Target under 10 ms round-trip latency between data centres in Hangzhou and Shanghai, about 170 km apart, over a direct fibre link.
cases.why: Light needs only about 2 ms for that round trip.

cases.proposal: A lab data logger writes 1 GB per day to a 1 TB SSD and uploads everything to the cloud once a month.
cases.why: About 30 GB per month into 1 TB.

cases.proposal: A quadcopter with 4 kg of total thrust and a 1 kg frame carries a 0.8 kg camera.
cases.why: Thrust-to-weight of about 2.2.

cases.proposal: Charge a 75 kWh electric car from 10% to 80% overnight (10 hours) using a 7 kW home charger.
cases.why: 52.5 kWh at 7 kW is about 7.5-8.5 hours.

cases.proposal: Serve a 7-billion-parameter language model quantized to 4 bits (about 4-5 GB of weights) on a GPU with 24 GB of memory, for a small internal team.
cases.why: Fits comfortably with room for context.

cases.proposal: Stream one 1080p security camera at 8 Mbps over a wired 100 Mbps Ethernet link inside a building.
cases.why: Uses under 10% of the link.
